newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.LANKA RUPEE ENDS UP ON WEAK DEMAND FOR DOLLARS.
newsitem.headline: S.LANKA RUPEE ENDS UP ON WEAK DEMAND FOR DOLLARS.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed firm against the dollar on Friday, due to low demand for the US unit, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.93 after opening at 58.95, they said.
"The market was very thin and there were plenty of dollars. This pushed the exchange rate close to the central bank's bottom," said an ABN Amro Bank dealer.
The central bank pushed up the dollar by three-quarter s of a local cent, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.9223 and 60.1127.
"Even speculators were quiet, as there is little room for the dollar to rise because of the good supply," said the ABN dealer.
Overnight call money rates closed at 11.5 percent, after opening at 9.5 percent, dealers said.
"Overnight call rates rose due to a lack of lenders. But that is a situation that should ease before long because the overall market seems liquid," said an American Express Bank dealer.
